correctness.rationale: For each integer \(n\ge4\) and every feasible nonuniform symmetric stochastic matrix, dihedral conjugation averaging cannot increase the operator norm from the stationary projector. The invariant family is \(P=(1-2a-b)I+a(S+S^{-1})+bS^n\). Its exact Fourier modes yield three linear SLEM lower constraints with strictly positive multipliers \(v/d\), \((w-u)/d\), \(v/d\), summing to one and annihilating both edge-weight variables. The resulting global lower bound is \((w-u)/d\). The proposed \(a=1/d\), \(b=(v-u)/d\) attains the three equalities. All other odd Fourier modes interpolate between the extremes, and every remaining even mode is bounded by a positive margin \(2v/d\) or \(2(v-2u)/d\). The identity \(v-2u=2u(1-u)>0\) for even \(n\ge4\) proves the last case. The holding probabilities are positive, and all three complementary equalities determine the unique invariant solution. Symbolic identities and the bundled 98-size, 30-LP/dense-spectrum, 980-dual-stress program were checked. Computation is corroboration, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The Möbius ladder family \(n\ge4\) has two distinct edge classes. Its parity-dependent exact optimum, three-mode sharp dual certificate, sixfold even-order gap gain and odd-order periodicity correction are not stated in the inspected relevant portions and full-text searches of the foundational 2004, 2005 and 2009 primary works or retrieved scientific-record results. The previously solved \(n=3\) edge-transitive \(K_{3,3}\) case is expressly excluded. These are claim/implication comparisons, not proof of exhaustive database uniqueness.

value.rationale: The exact globally optimal assignment applies to a natural non-edge-transitive cubic interconnection network for all integers \(n\ge4\). It exposes a topologically forced parity difference: equal-weight transitions are nonmixing for odd \(n\), while for even \(n\) their spectral gap is asymptotically a factor of \(6\) below the exact optimum. The three-mode certificate yields an explicit design principle for finite consensus and uniform-stationary random walks rather than an arbitrary finite computation, cosmetic substitution or known one-orbit graph result.
